title: רב חננאל ורב ברונא תלמידי רב
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: Rav Chananel and Rav Beruna, Rav's students. He sent the man who had lost his phylacteries to R. Abba bar Natan: Jerusalem Talmud, Megallechin. Abaye objected, and they consulted Chananel (Heilprin takes this Abaye to be the earlier one); see Rav Ika bar Avin. “R. Ika bar Avin said: R. Chananel said”; see there. Rav Beruna, his colleague. They asked Rav Huna, who told them, “Go ask Rav Chananel”: Bekhorot 24b. R. Zeira spoke in his name: Menachot 31b; Jerusalem Megillah 1:9 in the checked edition. And R. Chagra. Rav Chisda found Rav Chananel writing sacred books without a written exemplar. He said, “The whole Torah is worthy, etc.”: Megillah 18b, near the end. Tosafot, Moed Katan 19a, says he was a scribe. And R. Yeiva the Elder. And R. Yitzchak bar Abba Mechasya before Rav. “Rav said”—Pesachim 68a, 103a, near the end; Chagigah 13b. Rav—or some say Rabbah bar bar Chana—instructed Rav Chananel that he may write and sell in his usual manner to provide his livelihood: Moed Katan 19a, beginning. For his burial place, see R. Elazar ben Arakh. R. Yosha son of Rav Chananel: Jerusalem Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 11; there is some textual blurring there.
